releases.notes:
- Drag Beacon without losing your place: the pill now stays still while a quiet screen preview highlights where it will land.
- Dock Beacon vertically or horizontally in any corner, including vertically in the bottom-right.

- First launch now sets older inactive sessions aside as quiet history; resuming one brings it back automatically.
- A new hands-on walkthrough connects Beacon, proves an exact-session return, and teaches the lights, gear, and work timer by doing.
- Large Claude Desktop histories refresh with much less CPU work.
- Onboarding now ends with a hands-on practice pill: hover a light, open the gear, and try play/pause while each move checks itself off.

This beta tightens Beacon’s first-run experience and performance on Macs with existing agent history.

- Older inactive sessions are set aside as quiet history on first launch. If you resume one later, it returns to Beacon automatically.
- Setup stays in front, buttons respond on the first click, and the walkthrough visibly advances as soon as Beacon finds a real session.
- Large Claude Desktop histories refresh with much less CPU work.

- First launch now sets old inactive sessions aside as quiet history instead of filling the pill with a wall of lights; resuming one brings it back automatically.
- Setup stays in front while you open other apps, responds on the first click, and advances as soon as it finds a real session.
- Large Claude Desktop histories now refresh with much less CPU work.

- First launch now sets old inactive sessions aside as quiet history instead of filling the pill with a wall of lights; resuming one brings it back automatically.
- Setup now stays in front while you open Claude, Codex, or System Settings, and advances as soon as it finds a real session.
- Large Claude Desktop histories now refresh with much less CPU work.

- First launch now sets old inactive sessions aside as quiet history instead of filling the pill with a wall of lights; resuming one brings it back automatically.
- A new three-act setup explains the lights, checks Claude and Accessibility in place, and proves Beacon can return you to a real session.
- Large Claude Desktop histories now refresh with much less CPU work.
- Available updates now stay visible as a yellow sparkle beside the pill until you install or skip them, including after a restart or failed download.

- Hover over the corner pill for a gear that opens sessions, history, settings, and controls.
- Opening Beacon from Applications or Spotlight now brings that same window forward when macOS hides its menu-bar item.

- Beacon has a new graphite pilot-light design, with clearer idle, working, waiting, and ready-to-close states at every size.
- Switching between Claude and Codex now keeps the focus ring on the session actually in front, and automatic handoffs no longer drift to another app.
- Delegated agents stay grouped under their parent session, with a live count for background work and more detail on hover or in the session list.
- Hidden or continued sessions return when real work restarts, and stopping a work timer now responds immediately while its report finishes loading.

- Beacon now follows the exact Codex conversation you focus, so the “you’re here” ring and seen state stay with the right thread.
- Active Codex work stays yellow, and ordinary Codex green and yellow dots no longer show unhelpful question marks.
- Beacon can automatically hand off between visible Claude, Codex, editor, and terminal sessions when another session needs you or finishes.
- Orange takes priority over green, then blue; typing, switching sessions, or clicking a dot cancels the automatic hop.
- Automatic handoffs only open existing tabs, threads, or live terminals—they never import a duplicate session.
Clicking a pinned session now opens it, and a Codex dot goes to its thread.
A fresh install opens on today's work, not on every tab you ever left open. A finished Codex session says so once instead of forever.
The work timer now introduces itself to people who have never used it.
Report a problem now asks what went wrong and sends it — no folder, no homework.
Corrects Beacon's own usage reporting, and an orange session now says its piece once while you're working right there instead of flashing until you answer it.
Corrects Beacon's own usage reporting — no changes to what you see.

Updates now reach you within half an hour, with a menu-bar dot when one is waiting. Beacon also shares anonymous usage statistics (behaviour only, never your work) — one switch in Settings > Privacy & Data turns it off.
The first public build of Beacon.
